A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are developing a new theory of information consensus in networked systems that provides a unifying framework for analysis and design of consensus algorithms for a broad class of applications.

consensus algorithms provide a unified framework for analysis and design of distributed algorithms for cooperative control, information fusion, and distributed optimization in networked dynamic and static systems.
consensus and cooperation in networked dynamic multi-agent systems can be effectively analyzed and designed using tools from control theory and matrix analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the speed of consensus and the robustness of consensus algorithms are closely related to the spectral properties of the underlying network topology.

the consensus algorithms can provide rapid agreement and effective teamwork between all the participants in a networked system, and that the speed of convergence of the algorithms is closely related to the spectral properties of the networks.
